subject: sr-home-science
title: Model Question Paper 2
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 80 (with one optional module) · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: MCQs carry 1 mark; objective questions carry 2 marks.
Section B: very short answers 2 marks (30–50 words), short answers 3 marks (50–80 words), long answers 5 marks (80–120 words).
Attempt the questions of either Optional Module A (Housekeeping) or Optional Module B (Creative Hand Embroidery) in all sections.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or give reasons).

questions.q: Which four codes of ethics should be followed in a school?
questions.answer: Be regular and punctual; be polite and respectful to teachers and classmates; do your own work without copying or cheating; do not waste school resources and follow school rules.

questions.q: Which four food items can Anita include in her seven-month-old child's meal?
questions.answer: Mashed banana or potato, porridge, kheer and mashed dal or khichdi.

questions.q: Name the practices that cause air degradation and the one that causes land degradation. Choose from smoking, spitting, loud music, open defecation.
questions.answer: Air degradation: smoking and loud music. Land degradation: spitting and open defecation.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) Efficient use of equipment includes correct selection, operation and ________. (b) The foremost criterion for selecting equipment is that it must be ________ based.
Write the standardisation mark usually found on each: (i) paint (ii) honey (iii) canned juice (iv) pure wool shawl.

Identify two characteristics of language development in middle childhood. (a) Understanding that one word has more than one meaning (b) Having no vocabulary (c) Liking tongue twisters and metaphors (d) Unable to speak sentences.
Fill in the blanks. (a) The WHO defines adolescents as persons aged ________ years. (b) The legal age of marriage for boys is ________ years.
Write the full form of AIDS and HIV.
questions.answer: AIDS: Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome. HIV: Human Immunodeficiency Virus.

questions.q: Give single words. (a) Interlacing of two sets of yarns at right angles (b) Only one set of yarns interlooped (c) Weave with long floats and shine.
Fill in the blanks. (a) A ________ label gives characteristics such as size and variety. (b) The ________ Act, 1988 covers malpractices in selling textiles.

Give one word. (a) A collective name for white petrol, methylated spirit and benzene (b) A chemical used as a fabric whitener (c) A cleanser produced synthetically from chemicals (d) A natural oxidising bleach.
questions.answer: (a) Volatile (dry cleaning) solvents. (b) Blue. (c) Syndet. (d) Sunlight.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Name any two laws for consumer protection.
questions.answer: The Consumer Protection Act and the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (also the BIS Act and AGMARK Act).

questions.q: Why is the peer group important in middle childhood? Give two reasons.
questions.answer: It gives emotional security and comfort that adults cannot. It helps children compare themselves and become independent of parents.

questions.q: Mention two problems of adolescents.
questions.answer: Eating disorders such as undereating or overeating and suicidal tendencies from loneliness. Peer pressure and teenage pregnancy are also problems.

questions.q: Mention three ways in which poverty leads to juvenile delinquency.
questions.answer: Poor children lack facilities and find stealing easy. Parents may encourage them to steal or beg, and lack of play and education leads them into bad company.

or.q: Which three precautions should be adopted at the time of delivery?
or.answer: A skilled person should be present at delivery and a hospital referral should be possible. The newborn must be kept clean, the cord tied and cut hygienically, and breast-feeding started early.

questions.q: Why are knitted garments considered appropriate for winter wear?
questions.answer: Knitted wool has many air spaces which trap body heat. It is also stretchable and comfortable.

questions.q: Which three characteristics would you consider while buying clothes for summers?
questions.answer: The fabric should be absorbent like cotton. It should be light, loose and light-coloured and easy to launder.

or.q: Which three characteristics would you consider while buying clothes for your college-going sister?
or.answer: Fit and style that she likes, a mix-and-match combination for variety, and easy care and colour fastness.

questions.q: What is laundering? Name its steps in order (any five).
questions.answer: Laundering is washing, drying and finishing of clothes. The steps are mending, stain removal, sorting, soaking, washing, rinsing, starching or bluing, drying and ironing.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the advantages of non-conventional sources of energy (three points).
questions.answer: (i) They give a never-ending supply and are easily available. (ii) They are pollution free. (iii) They are locally produced, so low distribution cost, and small-scale units give jobs.

questions.q: Explain the role of the government in controlling environmental degradation (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Enforce strict pollution control laws and ensure waste treatment plants in industries. (ii) Provide efficient waste disposal and promote biogas and solar devices. (iii) Educate people, promote healthy farm practices and tree planting, and conserve wildlife.

questions.q: Explain how fuel can be conserved while cooking (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Soak pulses and cook in a pressure cooker, lowering the flame after the first whistle. (ii) Use separators to cook many dishes together and cover the pan. (iii) Clean burners and use a solar cooker when possible.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain any five investment avenues with their advantages.
questions.answer: (i) Bank: safe, interest, withdrawal and loans against fixed deposits. (ii) Post office: convenient, small amounts, tax-free interest in NSC. (iii) Provident Fund: compulsory saving, tax exemption and loans (GPF and PPF). (iv) Life insurance: safe, financial protection for dependents, tax relief and forced saving. (v) UTI units: regular dividend, tax relief and can be encashed. (vi) Shares and debentures: shares give possible high returns with risk; debentures give a fixed interest with more safety.

questions.q: Describe the energy options for the future with their advantages.
questions.answer: (i) Biogas from animal manure is a cheap fuel for cooking and lighting, and the sludge is a fertiliser. (ii) A solar cooker saves fuel and is safe. (iii) Solar cells give lighting and solar heating warms water and dries crops. (iv) Micro-hydel projects supply remote areas with low investment. (v) Wind energy is free and non-polluting and suits hilly areas. (vi) All are renewable, pollution free and give local jobs.

sections.title: Optional Module A (Housekeeping): Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or give reasons).

questions.q: True or False. (a) Acid should be rinsed immediately from ceramic tiles. (b) Carpets should be rolled up while damp.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: they should be dried thoroughly before rolling.

sections.title: Optional Module A (Housekeeping): Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: State two principles to be followed while using polishes.
questions.answer: Remove dust and dirt thoroughly before polishing and use small quantities. Rub off the polish thoroughly so the surface is not sticky.

questions.q: Why should a non-stick pan be rinsed immediately after use and cleaned with a sponge?
questions.answer: Hard scrubbers and steel wool scratch the Teflon coating. Rinsing at once and a sponge with soapy water keep it intact.

sections.title: Optional Module A (Housekeeping): Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the steps to clean a room daily (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Open the windows, remove unwanted articles and empty ash trays and dust bins. (ii) Sweep, dust furniture and brush or vacuum the carpet. (iii) Mop the floor, replace linen and survey the room.

sections.title: Optional Module B (Creative Hand Embroidery): Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Give two comparisons between stylised and geometrical design.
questions.answer: Stylised designs have more curves and details and are away from natural form; geometrical designs use simple shapes and straight lines. Stylised designs look decorative and complicated while geometrical ones look simple.

questions.q: Define tertiary colours with an example.
questions.answer: They are formed by mixing a primary and a secondary colour in equal quantity, such as blue and green gives blue-green.

sections.title: Optional Module B (Creative Hand Embroidery): Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the factors to be considered while planning an eco-friendly shopping bag.
questions.answer: (i) It must be light but strong with strong handles. (ii) The fabric must be water resistant, colour fast and non-absorbent such as canvas or jute. (iii) The embroidery must not snag and should suit all age groups.
